blocks.html: Mirsad Cerimovic, CAM, CMCA, AMS · July 6, 2026 · 4 min read

When boards interview management companies, they usually ask about responsiveness, financial reporting, and vendor relationships. They rarely ask about software — but they should. The platform a manager runs on determines how fast a work order moves, how transparent the financials are, and whether an owner can get an answer at 9 p.m. without calling anyone.

Stellar runs its portfolio on Portier369, an association management platform built specifically for condominiums and HOAs — not adapted from rental-property software. Here is what that means in practice for the communities we manage.
Owners get self-service, not phone tag

Every owner in a Stellar-managed community has a portal: pay assessments online, submit maintenance requests with photos, check account history, upload proof of insurance, and find governing documents — from a phone, with no app download required. The routine questions that used to be phone calls are now answered instantly.
Boards see the same numbers we do

Board members get their own workspace with live financial visibility — budgets versus actuals, receivables aging, and monthly statements — scoped to their association only. There is no waiting for a manager to export a report before a board meeting; the report is already there. That transparency is deliberate: we would rather answer questions about real numbers than be the only ones holding them.
These tools are part of our full condominium management service.

Illinois associations must handle rule enforcement carefully. The platform runs the entire violation lifecycle — photo documentation, notice generation, hearing scheduling, and fine assessment — so every case follows the same documented process. If a matter is ever challenged, the paper trail already exists.

Annual inspections, seasonal work, and vendor certificates are tracked on a preventive maintenance calendar with automated reminders. Chicago winters punish buildings that defer maintenance; a system that never forgets a boiler inspection is worth more than any brochure promise.

We evaluated the usual industry names. Most are rental-management platforms with an association module attached — you pay for leasing and tenant-screening tools a condo association will never use. Portier369 does one thing: community associations. The association accounting is true double-entry fund accounting, the portals cover every role from board member to vendor, and the pricing is flat per door with everything included.

For boards comparing management proposals: ask every candidate what platform they run on, whether owners and board members get their own portals, and whether financials are visible in real time. The software will shape your experience as much as the manager will.
